fields.h1: Build a Bug Report Form That Captures the Steps to Reproduce
fields.hero_description: Build a bug report form that collects steps to reproduce, the build and a screenshot, and sends each bug to the right queue.
fields.features_heading: What a Developer Needs to Reproduce a Bug
fields.features_subheading: "The button doesn't work" leaves a developer guessing which button and where. This form asks for the details up front.
fields.feature_1:
Numbered steps before the expected result

The form asks for numbered steps before anything else, then what the reporter expected and what happened instead. A developer reads three short answers in a fixed order.
fields.feature_2:
Browser, device, and build on every bug

Reporters pick the browser, operating system, and app build from lists you keep current. A bug filed against last month's build stands out before anyone tries to reproduce it.
fields.feature_3:
Screenshots saved with each bug

Reporters attach a screenshot or a short screen recording without leaving the form. Each file is stored with its report in a database you own and opens beside the steps.
fields.feature_4:
A severity level that decides who hears first

The reporter picks Critical, Major, Minor, or Low. Critical bugs post to a Slack channel or send an email the moment they are filed. Everything else waits for triage.
fields.feature_5:
An issue opened in the tracker for each bug

The app connects to GitHub or any other tracker with an API and opens an issue for every new bug. Its title, steps, build, and severity label arrive already filled in.
fields.feature_6:
The form's code, on your own servers

The form's full codebase exports to your GitHub repository on paid plans. Put the bug form inside your own product or host it anywhere, then keep building on the same code.

fields.usecase_heading: Who Files Bugs, and Where They Land
fields.tab_content_1:
Blank Safari exports come in with steps attached

Bookkeeper Rosalind Abernathy-Vale exports an invoice from Fernhallow Invoicing in Safari 18 and gets a blank PDF. On the bug report form she types 3 steps, attaches a screenshot, and marks the bug as happening every time. It lands in the support queue under Exports, steps in the order she took them.
fields.tab_content_2:
An Android crash goes into GitHub as issue #2187

Regression week at Sablewick Transit tests every screen on build 4.12.0. QA tester Anselm Thibodeaux finds that saving a trip with no return date closes the Android app. He writes down 4 steps and picks Major. The app opens GitHub issue #2187 with his steps, the build, and a Major label, and he goes back to testing.
fields.tab_content_3:
11 of 14 beta crashes, all on level 6

The Holmgaard Games puzzle beta runs on build 0.9.3. The form asks each player for the level, the device, and what they did right before the crash. In the first week, 14 crash reports come in. Producer Ines Marchetti-Cole sorts them by level and finds 11 of the 14 on level 6. Level 6 goes to the engineers first.
fields.tab_content_4:
Checkout breaks, and on-call hears it first

A customer writes to Copperlane Outfitters that checkout fails at the card step. Store manager Dashiell Okonkwo places a test order and hits the same error. He files the bug as Critical, and the app posts it to the #on-call channel in Slack. A Low bug filed that afternoon, a typo in the footer, waits for Thursday triage.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Bug Report Form
fields.howto_description: Follow these 7 steps to build a bug report form that gets clear steps from every reporter and routes each bug by severity.
fields.howto_step_1_des: Customers and QA testers need different versions of the form. A customer describes what they saw in plain words, while a tester can pick a build and a platform. Write down each group and where its bugs should go.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Mozilla's bug writing guidelines call steps to reproduce the most important part of any bug report. Number them and place them above every other field. Separate fields for the expected result and the actual result come next, one answer each.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Mozilla asks reporters to say whether they can reproduce the bug at will, occasionally, or not at all. Add that as a required choice. A bug that appears once in 20 tries needs a different plan from one that fails every time.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Pick the levels and write one line for each, such as Critical when checkout or sign-in is down. Then decide who hears about each level and how: a Slack post, an email, or a place in the weekly triage.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Put the fields and the severity rules in one prompt. Emergent builds the bug report form, the triage queue behind it, and the database that stores every bug. To change a field later, ask in plain English.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Connect GitHub or whichever tracker you already use for code work. The app opens an issue for each new bug through the tracker's API, carrying everything the reporter typed, so nobody copies text between two tabs.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 File two bugs as a test
fields.howto_step_7_des: File a Critical bug from a phone and a Low bug from a laptop. Check that the Critical one reaches on-call, the Low one waits for triage, and both issues list the steps in the order you typed them.

faq_plan.q: What is a bug report form?
faq_plan.a: A bug report form is a structured form that a customer or tester fills in when software does something wrong. It asks for the same details every time, starting with what happened and how to make it happen again. A developer can then try the steps without writing back first.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a bug report form?
faq_plan.a: List who will file bugs and the severity levels you use, then describe both in one prompt to Emergent's AI form builder. Emergent builds the form, a triage queue, and the database behind it. File one test bug at each severity before you share the link.

faq_plan.q: What fields should a bug report form template include?
faq_plan.a: Start with seven: a one-line summary, numbered steps, the expected result, the actual result, how often it happens, the browser or build, and a screenshot. Mozilla's guidelines also say to clearly separate facts (observations) from speculations. Give the reporter's guess about the cause its own optional field.

faq_plan.q: How do I keep billing complaints out of a bug report form?
faq_plan.a: Open the form with one question that asks what kind of problem it is. A customer who wants money back belongs on a refund request form, where the order number and amount come first. Only a problem with what the software did continues on to the steps.

faq_plan.q: Can one bug report form submission cover several bugs?
faq_plan.a: No. Mozilla's guidelines put it plainly: if you have multiple issues, please file separate bug reports. Each bug carries its own severity and status, and a combined report stays open until every part is fixed. Add a one-line note under the steps field asking for one bug per submission.

faq_plan.q: What makes a good title on a bug report form?
faq_plan.a: Name what broke, where, and under which condition, in one line: Invoice export is blank in Safari 18. Mozilla's guidelines say a good summary should quickly and uniquely identify a bug report. A title like Export broken fails that test, because ten other bugs could share it.

faq_plan.q: Should staff use a bug report form for laptop or access problems?
faq_plan.a: No. A broken laptop, a locked account, or a request for new software is IT work, and it belongs on an it request form. Keep the bug report form for software you build or sell, where the steps lead a developer to the code.

faq_plan.q: How do I add a bug report form to a mobile app?
faq_plan.a: Link the form from the app's help or settings screen, and ask for the device model, OS version, and app build as pick lists. The form opens in the phone's browser, and a screenshot attaches from the camera roll. Emergent builds it from a prompt and keeps every bug in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: Will a bug report form stop taking reports after a set number?
faq_plan.a: Not when Emergent builds it: Emergent forms have no response caps. Before a beta launch, check the limits of whichever form tool you use. One bad release can bring in a pile of crash reports in a single afternoon, and every one of them is worth keeping.

faq_plan.q: How should a bug report form handle sign-in problems?
faq_plan.a: Ask first whether the reporter can sign in at all. Someone who forgot a password needs a password reset form, not a developer. Link it from that question. When the sign-in page rejects a correct password, that is a real bug, and it should be filed as Critical.
